sourceRefs.title: Carrier 59SC5B-05SI: Installation, Start-up, Operating and Service and Maintenance Instructions

faultCodes.display: Red LED flashes 1 time, then 3 times
likelyCauses: Dirty filter or restricted duct system

faultCodes.display: Red LED flashes 1 time, then 4 times
Red LED flashes 2 times, then 2 times
likelyCauses: Flame is proved while gas valve is de-energized

faultCodes.display: Red LED flashes 2 times, then 3 times
Red LED flashes 2 times, then 4 times
Red LED flashes 3 times, then 1 time
faultCodes.meaning: Pressure switch did not close or reopened

faultCodes.display: Red LED flashes 3 times, then 3 times
likelyCauses: Dirty filter or restricted duct system

faultCodes.display: Red LED flashes 3 times, then 4 times
likelyCauses: defective flame sensor or loose connection

C13-S1.instruction: Check for a dirty air filter or restricted duct system.

C13-S2.instruction: Check if the vent is restricted or improperly sized.

C13-S3.instruction: Check the blower motor and wheel for looseness or defects.

C13-L1.instruction: Clean or replace filter / clear ducts

outcome.summary: Clean or replace dirty air filter and clear any restrictions in the duct system.
Clear restrictions from the vent or correct vent sizing issues.
Secure loose blower wheel or replace a defective blower motor.
Limit lockout cause not found in basic checks; perform advanced electrical and limit switch testing.

C14-S1.instruction: Check if there is a limit switch lockout or a flame rollout switch open.

C14-S2.instruction: Inspect limit or rollout switches and reset auto-reset after three hours.

outcome.summary: Clear limit switch or rollout switch trip condition and verify proper airflow.

C14-S3.instruction: Check for mis-wired gas valve or a defective control valve.

outcome.summary: Repair or correct the gas valve wiring harness.
Replace the faulty control valve.

C14-S7.instruction: Escalate for deeper diagnosis of control board or ignition components.

outcome.summary: Escalate for further electrical and control board diagnostics.

C22-S1.instruction: Check if the flame is proved while the gas valve is de-energized.

C22-S2.instruction: Inspect the gas valve for leaks or failure.

outcome.summary: Replace the stuck open or leaky gas valve.

C22-S3.instruction: Check control board operation and wiring.

outcome.summary: Escalate for deeper diagnosis of control board or wiring.

C23-S1.instruction: Check if the pressure switch contacts are stuck closed.

outcome.summary: Pressure switch is stuck closed and must be replaced.

C23-S3.instruction: Inspect pressure switch wiring and connections.

C23-S4.instruction: Repair or replace damaged wiring harness.

outcome.summary: Repair or replace damaged wiring connected to the pressure switch.

C23-S5.instruction: Escalate for deeper control board diagnosis.

outcome.summary: Switch and wiring check out; further diagnostic by qualified personnel is needed.

C24-S1.instruction: Inspect the 24V fuse on the control board.

C24-S2.instruction: Check for shorts in the 24V thermostat or accessory wiring.

C24-S3.instruction: Repair or replace the shorted wiring.

outcome.summary: Repair any damaged 24V wiring or shorted thermostat cables.

C24-S4.instruction: Replace the blown 3A automotive-type fuse with a new 3A fuse.

outcome.summary: Replace the open secondary voltage fuse with a new 3A fuse.

C24-S5.instruction: Verify control power status and LED operation.

C24-S6.instruction: Escalate for deeper control board diagnosis.

outcome.summary: The control board or internal transformer requires deeper electrical diagnosis.

C24-S7.instruction: Fault code 24 is cleared and normal operation is restored.

outcome.summary: Secondary voltage circuit is operating normally.

C31-S1.instruction: Check for excessive wind or restricted vent conditions.

options: excessive wind or vent restriction found

C31-S2.instruction: Clear the vent restriction or protect against excessive wind.

outcome.summary: Clear blocked vent or fix wind issue.

C31-S3.instruction: Inspect pressure switch tubing and condensate drainage.

C31-S4.instruction: Clear or reconnect pressure tubing and condensate drainage.

outcome.summary: Clear or secure pressure switch tubing and condensate lines.

C31-S5.instruction: Check inducer motor operation and voltage.

C31-S6.instruction: Repair or replace faulty inducer motor or wiring.

outcome.summary: Replace faulty inducer motor or correct voltage supply.
Replace pressure switch that fails to close or stays open.

C33-S1.instruction: Check air filter and duct system for restrictions or blockage.

C33-S2.instruction: Check venting system and combustion air supply for restrictions.

C33-S3.instruction: Inspect blower wheel and motor operation.

outcome.summary: Clean or replace dirty air filter and clear any restrictions in the duct system.
Remove obstructions from the venting system or combustion air intake.
Secure loose blower wheel or replace a defective blower motor.
Perform a physical limit switch check per manual instructions or test limit control operation.

C34-S1.instruction: Measure the flame current signal from the flame sensor during burner operation.

C34-S2.instruction: Clean the flame sensor with fine steel wool and inspect wiring connections.

outcome.summary: Clean oxide buildup off the flame sensor with fine steel wool.

C34-S3.instruction: Check if gas supply is turned on and gas pressure is adequate.

C34-S4.instruction: Inspect control ground and wiring harness.

outcome.summary: Check control ground continuity and ensure green/yellow wire is connected to furnace sheet metal.

C34-S5.instruction: Open the manual gas shut-off valve.

outcome.summary: Open manual shut-off valve to restore gas supply.

safetyStops.message: Stop. Possible gas leak. Don't operate switches or the furnace. Leave the area, then follow your company's gas leak procedure and call the gas utility.
Stop. Possible carbon monoxide. Get everyone outside to fresh air, leave the furnace off, and call 911 from outside.
Stop. Possible overheating or fire. Shut off power at the disconnect and don't restart until the cause is found and fixed.
Stop. Water near live electrical parts. Shut off power at the disconnect before touching anything and dry the area first.
Stop. Exposed or damaged wiring. Shut off and lock out power before going any further.
Stop. Flame rollout is a fire hazard. Shut off gas and power. Don't reset the rollout switch until the heat exchanger and venting are inspected.
